newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ahold to run shops at Dutch Shell stations.
newsitem.headline: Ahold to run shops at Dutch Shell stations.

text.p: Retailer Koninklijke Ahold NV said on Wednesday it would open small-scale Albert Heijn food shops at most of Shell's 750 petrol stations in the Netherlands.
"The agreement follows successful testing of the concept in three Dutch cities," Ahold said in a statement.
The franchise shops will be situated by Shell while Ahold's subsidiary Albert Heijn will design and stock them. Initial plans call for about 50 shops to be opened this year.
"The agreement is a win-win situation which will benefit both companies and the Dutch consumer," Albert Heijn director Jan Andreae said in the statement.
Albert Heijn is the Netherlands' leading supermarket chain with 640 outlets across the country.
Ahold has worldwide annual sales of about $24 billion and employs 190,000 people.
